claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has useful room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance during high-temperature air exposure.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
The proposed intervention is pack cementation aluminizing using a powder pack containing 5–10 wt% Al at approximately 900 °C for about 3 hours.
Pack cementation aluminizing will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminizing treatment will cause aluminum to diffuse into the alloy surface.
Diffused aluminum will generate an aluminide-enriched surface layer on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide-enriched surface layer will oxidize preferentially to form a continuous, dense Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reduced oxygen diffusion through the scale will retard further oxidation and pesting.
Relative to untreated material, treated specimens will have lower oxidation mass gain during high-temperature air exposure.
Relative to untreated material, treated specimens will avoid pesting-related degradation during high-temperature air exposure.
The aluminizing treatment and subsequent exposure will leave room-temperature ductility largely unchanged.
The aluminizing treatment and subsequent exposure will leave high-temperature yield strength largely unchanged.
The proposed oxidation-protection hypothesis applies to air exposures between approximately 800 and 1000 °C for around 5 hours.
Mechanical-property retention is to be assessed at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
